_meta.description: Equipment catalog for Mutants & Masterminds 4e character creation. All 'description' fields are short, original text written for this project's UI (always-visible label copy), not taken from the rulebook. Mechanical fields (category, cost, costKind, effects, modifiers, grants, critical, patterns, implementation) reflect game rules/facts, not copyrighted prose. Companion to docs/design-data/equipment-design.json (the full design reference, including per-item notes and the vehicle/installation trait tables) and docs/mm-equipment-design.md.

currency.name: Equipment Point
currency.note: Equipment is a bundle of power effects carried at the top tier of the Removable flaw. Rather than applying that flaw item by item, the Equipment advantage hands out 5 Equipment Points per rank and items are priced at their undiscounted effect cost. The flaw's limitations still apply in play even though its discount is not recomputed.
currency.reconfigure: At the start of each adventure, or between scenes with access to a headquarters or cache.
currency.notAPower: Equipment does not count as a power. A character built purely from equipment can still be described as having no powers.

categoryKey.utility: A small gadget, mostly built from the Feature effect or a low-rank utility effect
categoryKey.close_weapon: A hand-held weapon used in close combat
categoryKey.ranged_weapon: A projectile, thrown, or energy weapon
categoryKey.accessory: An add-on fitted to another weapon rather than used on its own
categoryKey.grenade: A thrown area attack, consumed on use
categoryKey.explosive: A placed area attack, consumed on use
categoryKey.armor: Worn protection, normally a Protection effect
categoryKey.shield: A carried defence granting Enhanced Defense; requires active use
categoryKey.kit: A bundle or array of other items, priced as a build rather than a fixed line
categoryKey.vehicle: A built platform with its own Size/Strength/Toughness/Defense/Speed trait costs
categoryKey.installation: A built fixed structure with its own Size/Toughness/Feature trait costs

_meta.equipmentCategoriesNote: How the character sheet's Equipment block groups its cards, in display order. 'id' matches an item's 'category'; 'title' is the heading shown above that group. A mod adding a category should add a row here so its items get a group of their own instead of being folded into the last one.

costKindKey.ranked: Cost varies over a small number of defined ranks
costKindKey.built: Assembled from components or trait tables; no single printed cost

stackingRule.rule: Equipment bonuses do not stack with each other or with bonuses from other sources — only the single highest applicable bonus applies.
stackingRule.engineNote: Compute equipment contributions as max(), not sum(), per target stat, and then take max() again against non-equipment sources. This is why a character with high native Protection gains nothing from armour.

strengthBasedDamage.baseRule: A Strength-Based Damage effect adds the wielder's Strength rank to the weapon's Damage rank.
strengthBasedDamage.costPerRankDivisor: When modifiers push the effect above 1 point per rank, divide the wielder's Strength rank by the effect's cost per rank and round down; that reduced number is the Strength bonus actually added. An effect costing 1 point per rank or less adds Strength unmultiplied, and flat modifiers never trigger the divisor because they do not change the cost per rank.

breakage.rule: An ordinary weapon can only carry Strength up to its own Toughness. Exerting more Strength than that breaks the weapon when it is used — a real event at the table, so the character generator warns rather than silently capping the bonus.
breakage.materialToughnessNote: Toughness by the material an item's 'implementation.material' names, from the printed guidance (roughly 4 for wooden weapons, 7-8 for metal). An item naming no material, or one this table does not list, is never warned about.

_meta.vehicleClassesNote: Which movement effect a stock vehicle's printed Speed rank is a rank of, so a plane's Speed reaches the sheet as Flight and a boat's as Swimming. An Exotic vehicle names no default: it carries its own 'movement' block instead.

vehicleSizeExtension.note: Beyond size rank 5, each further rank adds +2 Strength, +1 Toughness, and -1 Defense (GM option). The table is extended arithmetically rather than storing extra rows.

vehicleCombat.defenseRank: A moving vehicle's Defense rank equals its current speed rank plus the Defense modifier for its Size.
vehicleCombat.stationary: A stationary vehicle can be attacked as a routine check at DC 10 plus the vehicle's Defense modifier.

installationTraits.note: An installation starts at size rank 5 (a house) and Toughness 6 for nothing; size costs 1 Equipment Point per rank up (and refunds 1 per rank down), Toughness 1 per +2, and each Feature 1. The printed trait table gives Size a starting rank of 0, which contradicts both the surrounding text and the size table itself (rank 11 = 6 points, rank 1 = -4, i.e. exactly sizeRank - 5); rank 5 is used.

installationPowerLevel.note: An installation has no defences other than its Toughness, so its Toughness may reach twice the series Power Level while Impervious stays capped at the Power Level itself. That is a different cap pair from a character's.
